{"review_id":"r1-safety_bypass","slice":"WP-SCP-024/024B-core","lens":"safety_bypass","reviewer":"sonnet-r1-safety_bypass","date":"2026-05-09","verdict":"CHANGES_REQUESTED","summary":"The 024B-core safety-bypass review surfaces one CRIT and two MAJ findings plus downstream MIN/nit. SBP-CRIT-001 is the dominant risk: check-invocation-log-entry.sh uses a two-pass cascade-status extraction where the first pass (dispatch_note_mode, line 127) allows leading whitespace via r'(?m)^[ \\t]*cascade-status:' and uses re.search (first-match). A DISPATCH-NOTE containing any indented '  cascade-status: not applicable' line before the real cascade-status declaration makes dispatch_note_mode='not applicable' → exits 0 with 'nothing to enforce', bypassing all four invariant-2 enforcement paths (log-entry presence, target-match, TF-regex, log-not-modified negative assertion for blocked-on-adopter-conflict). SBP-MAJ-001 is an independent bypass: when --branch-protection-log receives an absolute path with --diff-base, normalize_path (os.path.normpath, line 103) keeps the value absolute while git diff --name-only returns repo-relative paths; grep -Fxq at line 192 never matches, silently setting branch_log_modified=0. For blocked-on-adopter-conflict, the log-not-modified assertion always passes even when the log was actually changed. SBP-MAJ-002 flags the 'not applicable' case branch at lines 157-160 as unreachable dead code — second-pass regex ([a-z-]+) never captures strings with spaces — creating false confidence in a second defensive handler that does not exist. Template permissions ceiling (contents:read + statuses:write only, no id-token, no attestations), fork-PR if: clause, Renovate marker, scaffold denylist applied post-readlink/realpath, bootstrap-only guard at line 48 before any exit-2 code (line 154), SHA non-existence exit 2, parse_entry_repo exactly-one assertion, and slug canonicalization all pass their respective safety checks. Test harness uses env -i isolation and EXIT-trap cleanup with no network calls beyond the fake-gh shim.","findings":[{"id":"SBP-CRIT-001","severity":"CRIT","claim":"First-pass regex at line 127 allows leading whitespace: r'(?m)^[ \\t]*cascade-status:\\s+...' + re.search first-match. A DISPATCH-NOTE with '  cascade-status: not applicable' (any leading whitespace) before 'cascade-status: onboarded' sets dispatch_note_mode='not applicable' → exits 0 ('nothing to enforce') before second-pass enforcement runs. All four invariant-2 check-paths bypassed.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:127 re.search(r'(?m)^[ \\t]*cascade-status:\\s+([^\\r\\n]+?)\\s*$', text) captures first occurrence regardless of leading indent. Lines 133-136: if dispatch_note_mode='not applicable' then exit 0. Lines 138-258 (cascade_status extraction + all enforcement paths) never reached. No test covers indented-not-applicable before real cascade-status.","impact":"All four enforcement paths silently bypassed (exit 0 + 'nothing to enforce' message). No log entry required; no target match checked; TF-regex not enforced; blocked-on-adopter-conflict log-modification assertion not run. Any cascade PR passes CI by prepending one indented '  cascade-status: not applicable' line to its DISPATCH-NOTE.","mitigation":"Remove '[ \\t]*' from the first-pass regex at line 127: change r'(?m)^[ \\t]*cascade-status:\\s+([^\\r\\n]+?)\\s*$' to r'(?m)^cascade-status:\\s+([^\\r\\n]+?)\\s*$'. Both passes then share the same strict line-start anchor. Alternatively, remove the first pass entirely and handle not-applicable as a recognised value in the second-pass case statement (requires fixing SBP-MAJ-002 first)."},{"id":"SBP-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"When --branch-protection-log is given as an absolute path with --diff-base, normalize_path (os.path.normpath, line 103) keeps the value absolute; git diff --name-only at line 187 returns repo-relative paths; grep -Fxq at line 192 never matches → branch_log_modified=0 always. For blocked-on-adopter-conflict, the log-not-modified assertion silently passes even when the log was actually modified.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:103 normalize_path = os.path.normpath (not relative-ised). Line 187: git diff --name-only returns 'docs/reviews/.../branch-protection-log.md'. Line 192: grep -Fxq '/abs/path/.../branch-protection-log.md' fails against relative entry → branch_log_modified=0. Test case 18 uses a double-slash path (stays relative after normpath) and passes, masking the absolute-path variant.","impact":"blocked-on-adopter-conflict negative assertion (log NOT modified) passes falsely when log was modified, because branch_log_modified=0. Attacker declares conflict-close while actually invoking enable-required-check.sh and modifying the log; CI passes. Requires passing --branch-protection-log as an absolute path — unusual but undocumented as invalid input.","mitigation":"Compute the log path relative to REPO_ROOT before the grep comparison: relpath=\"${BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG_REAL#${REPO_ROOT}/}\"; grep -Fxq \"$relpath\" <<<\"$changed_files\". Alternatively, reject absolute --branch-protection-log values outright, since git diff --name-only always returns repo-relative paths."},{"id":"SBP-MAJ-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The 'not applicable') case branch at lines 157-160 in case \"$cascade_status\" is unreachable dead code. Second-pass regex ([a-z-]+) at line 145 cannot capture strings containing spaces; 'not applicable' can never be assigned to $cascade_status. The dead branch creates false confidence in a second defensive handler for SBP-CRIT-001's bypass path — no such handler exists.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:145 re.findall(r'^cascade-status:\\s+([a-z-]+)\\s*$', ...) — [a-z-]+ is strictly [a-z] and hyphen; space excluded. For 'cascade-status: not applicable', findall returns []; script exits 1 via set -e before reaching case. Lines 157-160 'not applicable') branch therefore never entered under any reachable execution path.","impact":"Apparent two-layer defense (first-pass early-exit + case branch) reduces to single layer. After SBP-CRIT-001 exploits the first-pass, the case branch provides no fallback. Code reviewers may incorrectly conclude a second handler closes the bypass surface, reducing urgency to fix SBP-CRIT-001.","mitigation":"Remove the unreachable 'not applicable') case branch (lines 157-160). After fixing SBP-CRIT-001, document that not-applicable detection is single-pass with strict line-start anchor. If defense-in-depth is desired, extend cascade_status regex to capture 'not applicable' as a valid multi-word value and re-add the case branch."},{"id":"SBP-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"D-044 (docs/DECISIONS.md) describes 'cascade-status: not applicable → exit 0' without documenting the two-pass architecture or the leading-whitespace first-pass regex. An operator or auditor citing D-044 for safety properties of the not-applicable carve-out cannot discover the SBP-CRIT-001 bypass surface from the decision record alone.","evidence":"D-044 rationale states 'cascade-status: not applicable → exit 0' and 'exactly-one-match assertion (closes multi-occurrence injection bypass)'. No mention of dispatch_note_mode first pass, re.search first-match semantics, or ^[ \\t]* leading-whitespace tolerance. The exactly-one assertion claim is accurate for the second-pass enforcement but silent on the first-pass bypass surface.","impact":"Trust-model inaccuracy enables future operators to cite D-044 as evidence that not-applicable detection is secure, missing the leading-whitespace escape hatch. Adversarial review rounds citing D-044 for coverage of the multi-occurrence bypass may conclude the class is fully closed when SBP-CRIT-001 remains open.","mitigation":"Fix SBP-CRIT-001 (making D-044's implicit trust accurate by eliminating the bypass). Additionally amend D-044 to state that not-applicable detection uses a single strict-start-of-line regex, preventing future re-introduction of the leading-whitespace pattern as a silent regression."},{"id":"SBP-MIN-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh has no regression test for DISPATCH-NOTE with '  cascade-status: not applicable' (indented, first occurrence) before 'cascade-status: onboarded'. Test case 14 confirms indented same-value duplicates are tolerated (exit 0) but does not guard the bypass class. SBP-CRIT-001 has no regression gate in the test suite.","evidence":"test case 14 DISPATCH-NOTE: '  cascade-status: onboarded\\ncascade-status: onboarded', expects exit 0 — confirming indented lines are tolerated. No test uses '  cascade-status: not applicable\\ncascade-status: onboarded'. Pre-fix this exits 0 (bypass); post-fix should exit non-zero (enforcement fires or dispatch_note_mode mismatch).","impact":"SBP-CRIT-001 fix can be silently re-introduced in a future refactor without test failure. CI gives false confidence that indented cascade-status variants are handled correctly for all combinations relevant to safety.","mitigation":"Add test: DISPATCH-NOTE = '  cascade-status: not applicable\\ncascade-status: onboarded\\n- **Target:** jrnb2024/pim\\n' with branch-protection-log modified; expect non-zero exit after SBP-CRIT-001 fix. This test fails before fix (exposes the bypass) and passes after fix (proves regression guard active)."},{"id":"SBP-nit-001","severity":"nit","claim":"scaffold-downstream.sh lines 142-146: first case block denies /private/var/tmp|/private/var/tmp/* only. Second case block (lines 148-152) already covers /private/var|/private/var/* — a strict superset. The first block fires before the second but matches no path that the second does not also match; it is dead code with an identical die message.","evidence":"scaffold-downstream.sh:142-146 case $OUTPUT_DIR in /private/var/tmp|/private/var/tmp/*). Lines 148-152 include /private/var|/private/var/* which subsumes all /private/var/tmp/* paths. Both blocks emit identical error string. No path exists that matches the first block without matching the second.","impact":"Dead code; no functional security gap today. If the second case block is edited to carve out an exception for a /private/var/* subpath, the first block would silently fail to provide backup coverage for /private/var/tmp specifically.","mitigation":"Remove lines 142-146 (first case block). Consolidate all denylist patterns in the single second case block to eliminate maintenance divergence and the false layering impression."},{"id":"SBP-nit-002","severity":"nit","claim":"canonicalize_adopter_slug (lines 93-99) collapses dots and underscores to hyphens: 'org/repo.foo' and 'org/repo-foo' both yield 'org-repo-foo'. No runtime collision detection exists. A slug collision causes TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-<slug> regex to match the wrong adopter's STATUS.md or DISPATCH-NOTE row, producing a false-positive pass.","evidence":"Lines 95-98: re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9-]+', '-', s) normalises all non-[a-z0-9-] chars including dots and underscores to hyphens. 'jrnb2024/repo.foo' and 'jrnb2024/repo-foo' both yield 'jrnb2024-repo-foo'. Current 5-cohort repos (pim, recommender, shopify-app, mapp-doc-agent, control-tower) have no collisions. Plan-doc §2 states uniqueness-per-cohort but provides no runtime enforcement.","impact":"False-positive TF row match for wrong adopter when slugs collide; STATUS.md check passes for adopter B because adopter A's correctly-formatted TF row matches the derived regex. Low risk for current fixed 5-cohort; elevated if cohort expands to repos with name variants.","mitigation":"Document the uniqueness precondition in the function header. For future cohort expansion, add a pre-authoring collision check validating no existing TF row in STATUS.md or branch-protection-log matches the new slug before onboarding proceeds."}]}
